## Lovable GitHub connection not working: sync, missing commits and reconnect fixes

GitHub is N commits ahead of Lovable · Lovable and GitHub have diverged · This repository is no longer accessible

You connected your Lovable project to GitHub and it doesn't work. Clicking Connect GitHub does nothing, the commits you push never show up in Lovable, or the project's GitHub settings say GitHub is N commits ahead of Lovable, Lovable and GitHub have diverged or This repository is no longer accessible. Each message has its own cause. The usual reflex, disconnecting and connecting again, often makes things worse. Here's how to find the cause and fix it.

## First, how the connection works

Lovable keeps two separate links, and each problem breaks one of them:

- The workspace connection: the Lovable GitHub App, installed on your GitHub account or organization. One connection serves every project in the workspace, so when it breaks, they all stop syncing.

- The project link: one Lovable project, one GitHub repository and one branch at a time, by default the repository's default branch (usually main).

Open Project settings → Git → GitHub, or the + button next to the chat input, then Project → GitHub. The status and the sync card there tell you which section below to read.

Don't disconnect the project to "reset" it. The Reconnect button Lovable shows when the connection has a problem is safe: it restores access to the same repository. But Disconnect followed by Connect never relinks your repository. Lovable creates a brand-new one, and the old one stays on GitHub, unlinked, with its history.

Only want a copy of your code? You don't need GitHub for that: on paid plans, use Download codebase in Project settings → Git.

## 1. "Connect GitHub" does nothing, or there's no GitHub option

- Nothing happens when you click Add account or Connect GitHub. Your browser blocked the GitHub popup. Allow popups for Lovable and click again.

- No GitHub card in Project settings → Git. The project already syncs with GitLab or Bitbucket. A project links to one provider at a time, and the GitHub card only appears after you disconnect the other one.

- You can't add or change the connection. Only a workspace owner or admin can install the GitHub App and add a workspace connection. Connecting or disconnecting a project takes a workspace or project owner or admin. Editors can see the sync status and switch branches, nothing more. Ask the workspace owner.

- Your organization's connection isn't in the list. If someone else installed the Lovable GitHub App on an organization you're not a member of, you won't see it. Ask them to add you to the organization, or to set up the workspace connection themselves.

## 2. You want Lovable to use a repository you already have

Lovable can't link a project to an existing repository. Git sync always creates a new one, private by default, in the account or organization you pick. To bring existing code in:

- On the repository's GitHub page, click Code → Download ZIP.

- In Lovable, import it with Upload code. This copies the code into a new project.

- Connect GitHub to that new project. Lovable creates a fresh repository and keeps it in sync from then on.

The ZIP carries your files, not your commit history: the original repository keeps that.

## 3. Your commits don't show up in Lovable

Check the branch first. Lovable syncs only the branch shown in the branch picker of its GitHub settings. Commits anywhere else, such as a feature branch or a pull request that isn't merged, never come back into Lovable. Either merge them into that branch (for example, merge your pull request into main), or select their branch in the picker: Lovable then edits and syncs that branch instead.

If you did push to the synced branch and the sync card says GitHub is N commits ahead of Lovable, Lovable missed GitHub's notice about your push. Lovable pulls changes when GitHub notifies it of a push, and it won't fetch a missed push later on its own. Reconnect doesn't help, and Re-check only compares the two sides. What works is a new push to the synced branch, even an empty one:

git commit --allow-empty -m "Trigger Lovable sync"
git push

Lovable then syncs the branch to its current state on GitHub, earlier commits included. Before you push, make sure your latest Lovable edits are already on GitHub. If the card says the two sides have diverged, read section 4 first.

## 4. "Lovable and GitHub have diverged", or a lovable-sync branch appeared

Both sides have commits the other doesn't. Maybe you kept editing in Lovable while someone pushed to the same branch, or a branch protection rule refused Lovable's push. So that nothing is lost, Lovable pushes its changes to a branch named lovable-sync and shows Your changes conflict with commits on <your branch> and could not be merged automatically. To fix it:

- On GitHub, open the lovable-sync branch and review what Lovable changed.

- Merge it into your synced branch with a pull request, and resolve any conflicts there.

Watch out: the next sync from GitHub replaces Lovable's version of the branch with GitHub's. Edits made only in Lovable disappear from the project if they never reached GitHub. Lovable saves a backup first, and the project owner can restore it. If a later push is refused too, Lovable adds it to the same lovable-sync branch, or to a new lovable-sync-<timestamp> branch if you've committed to lovable-sync yourself.

## 5. Lovable shows a Reconnect prompt

When the workspace connection breaks, the project's GitHub settings show Reconnect with one of these messages. A workspace owner or admin fixes it once, and every project on that connection resumes.

- The Lovable GitHub App is suspended. Click Reconnect. The app's settings on GitHub open in a new tab: unsuspend it there.

- Lovable no longer has access to this repository. Someone limited the app to Only select repositories and left yours out. Click Reconnect, then under Repository access choose All repositories or add your repository.

- Install the GitHub App for … to enable gitsync. This usually follows a workspace transfer, or a removed workspace connection. Click Reconnect and reinstall the app on the account or organization GitHub shows. Lovable relinks the project by itself.

- The Lovable GitHub App has been uninstalled. This one costs more. Uninstalling the app disconnected every project that used it and removed the workspace connection. Reinstall it from Workspace settings → Git → GitHub → Add connection, then click Connect in each project. Each project gets a new repository; the old ones stay on GitHub with their history.

## 6. "This repository is no longer accessible"

The repository was deleted, or transferred to an account or organization your workspace has no connection for. Two ways out:

- Undo it on GitHub. Restore the deleted repository (GitHub's guide: Restoring a deleted repository), or transfer it back to its first owner. Sync resumes by itself.

- Start a new repository. Disconnect the project in its GitHub settings, then connect it again. Lovable creates a new repository with your current code.

Renaming doesn't cause this. Some older answers say a rename breaks the sync for good, but Lovable's current docs say a renamed repository, account or organization keeps syncing and Lovable updates the link itself. A transfer keeps syncing only if your workspace also has a GitHub connection for the new owner, so add that connection first, then transfer.

## 7. Other things that stop the sync

- A lovable-fallback branch appeared. Someone deleted the synced branch on GitHub, so Lovable moved the project to a new lovable-fallback branch to keep you editing. Pick another branch or recreate the original one. Once you've switched away, you can delete lovable-fallback.

- "Your project contains files that exceed the maximum file size limit (100 MB)". GitHub refuses files over 100 MB. Delete the listed files, or ask Lovable to remove them, and let the sync retry. If it still fails, the file is stuck in the history and Lovable Support has to clean it up.

- A big file syncs in, but Lovable can't change it. Lovable can't save files over 10 MB. For images and video, ask Lovable to "Migrate large files to CDN assets".

- You want the project on another GitHub account. There's no switch. Disconnect, then connect again with the other installation: Lovable creates a new repository there.

## Still stuck?

Check status.lovable.dev: during a Lovable incident, sync can stop for everyone. Then compare the sync card in Project settings → Git → GitHub with your repository's commit list on GitHub. Lovable's own commits come from lovable-dev[bot], so you can tell which side has what. If the two still don't match after a new push to the synced branch, contact Lovable Support.

guides.t: Lovable preview not working: not loading, blank or stale
guides.d: Lovable preview won't load, stays white or shows an old version? What each message means, three refreshes to try in order, and what to tell Lovable.
p: preview has not been built yet
guides.x:
Fix guide · updated 2026-11-11

## Lovable preview not working (not loading, blank, or not updating)

preview not loading · white preview · not updating · « Preview has not been built yet »

The preview pane spins forever, stays white, shows an error, or still shows your app from three changes ago. Lovable's own engineering blog explains why this happens: the preview "is not a static page. It is a real developer server running your real app". That server runs in a temporary cloud environment that Lovable starts for your project. So a broken preview means one of two things. Either that environment isn't running, or it's running and your app crashes inside it. The message in the pane usually tells you which one.

## First: what does the preview say?

Find your case in this list. The meanings and fixes come from Lovable's preview documentation.

- "Still building?" with a Keep building button: the environment paused because you were away for a while. Click Keep building. Lovable says this is normal and changes nothing in your project or on your live site.

- "Starting live preview…" for several minutes: Lovable is still starting it. It retries a failed start by itself, and if your device went offline it waits for the connection to come back. You don't need to refresh. If the message stays, check your internet connection.

- "Live preview couldn't start": the start failed even after the automatic retries. Check your connection, then click Try again. If the message comes back, restart the environment with Shift + Refresh (section 1). If an earlier version is available, Dismiss shows that version for now.

- "Live preview lost connection": the link to the environment broke, for example when your device went offline. Do the same as above: check your connection, then Try again, then Shift + Refresh.

- "Live preview stopped responding": the environment started, but your app stopped answering, or crashed again after Lovable restarted it. Click Try again once. If the message returns, the cause is in your app's code, so go to section 2.

- "Preview has not been built yet": this one isn't in Lovable's docs. Taken literally, it means the build behind the preview hasn't finished. Give it a minute. If it doesn't clear, treat it like "couldn't start": check your connection, then Try again, then Shift + Refresh.

- A white page with no message: the environment is running and your app crashes before it draws anything. Go to section 2.

- The preview works but shows an old version: go to section 3.

## 1. The three refreshes, in this order

- Refresh, the button above the preview. It reloads the page inside the pane.

- Shift + Refresh: hold Shift while you click the same button. This also restarts the preview environment, and Lovable's docs say it "resolves most loading issues".

- A hard browser refresh: Cmd+Shift+R on Mac, Ctrl+Shift+R on Windows and Linux. It reloads the whole editor without using what your browser kept from earlier visits.

If none of the three works, open the project in a private window, where extensions are usually off. If the preview works there, one of your browser extensions is in the way, often an ad blocker or a privacy blocker. Turn your extensions off one at a time to find it.

## 2. White preview, or "stopped responding": your app is crashing

Lovable's docs: "A blank preview usually comes from an error in the app itself." The environment is fine. Your app's code throws an error before anything appears on screen. You fix that in the code, not with more refreshes.

The quick way. Ask Lovable in the project chat, using the exact wording its docs suggest:

The preview is white, investigate and fix it.

or, for the other message:

The preview shows "Live preview stopped responding", investigate and fix it.

If a build error appeared while Lovable was working, there is also a Try to fix button on the activity card. Your first fixes there are free. See Lovable's Try to fix button for how it works and when it starts using credits.

The sure way: read the real error yourself. Click Open in new tab above the preview. That opens your development preview in its own tab, and you need to be logged in to Lovable to see it. Right-click the page → Inspect → Console, reload, and copy the first red line. Three red lines you'll often see:

- Failed to resolve import "…" from "src/…". Does the file exist?: the code imports a file or a package that isn't there. Maybe it was renamed, deleted, or never installed.

- Uncaught TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading '…'): the code uses something that doesn't exist yet. Usually that's data that hasn't loaded, or a field with a different name.

- supabaseUrl is required.: the app creates its Supabase connection with an empty address. A setting it reads is missing where the preview runs.

Paste that line into the chat. With the exact error, Lovable fixes the cause. With "it's broken", it guesses.

If it worked an hour ago, find the last version that worked before you change anything. Each of Lovable's replies in the chat has a Preview action that shows your app as it was right after that message, without reverting anything. Go back through them until one works. Then either revert to that version from version history, or tell Lovable which message last worked and ask it to compare. If the preview breaks again right after the same kind of request, try Plan mode before rebuilding, so Lovable explains its approach before it writes code.

A build error can also stop you from publishing. Lovable blocks publishing while the latest build fails. See Lovable build unsuccessful.

## 3. The preview doesn't show your latest change

Check these in order. Each one takes a few seconds.

- Lovable is still working. The preview updates as Lovable builds, so a change only appears once Lovable has made it. Wait until the activity in the chat has finished, then click Refresh.

- Live preview is turned off. Look in Project settings → General → Preview. With Live preview off, the pane shows the most recent completed version and only updates when Lovable finishes a change, not while it works. That's by design. Turn it back on if you want to watch changes appear.

- You're looking at an earlier version. If you clicked Preview on an older chat message, or opened a version in history, the pane shows that version. Go back to the latest one.

- You're on a draft, or on the main version. Each draft has its own preview at its own web address. A change made on a draft doesn't show in the main project's preview, and the other way around.

- You're looking at the published site. Your live site is a copy that only changes when you publish. If the preview shows the change and your live address doesn't, click Publish, then Publish changes. If it's the other way around, see Lovable published site not working (but the preview works).

- Your browser kept an old copy. Do the hard refresh from section 1.

## 4. A preview link you shared doesn't open

- You sent the "Open in new tab" address. That address requires a Lovable login with access to your project, so it won't open for anyone else. To show your app to someone, use Share → Share a preview link. Anyone with that link can view the app without a Lovable account.

- The link expired. On Free and Pro plans, preview links expire after 7 days. Make a new one. On Business and Enterprise plans, you choose the expiry (24 hours, 7 days, 30 days or never), and you can add a password. If you did, the other person needs it too.

- Your company turned them off. Enterprise workspaces can disable shared preview links completely.

A preview link always shows your latest in-progress version. To give someone a stable address that doesn't change while you work, publish the app.

## 5. When the problem is Lovable, not your app

Every project you open has the same problem, even a brand-new empty one? Then the problem is probably on Lovable's side. Check status.lovable.dev. If there's an incident, wait. Every change you make while the preview is broken has to be checked again afterwards. If the status page is green and a new empty project fails too, Lovable's docs say paid plans can contact Support. Send them the exact message in the pane and the time it started.

## What to send Lovable

Whether you ask the chat or ask support, five lines get a better answer than a screenshot alone:

The preview shows: [the exact message, or "a white page"]
It started after: [your last request, or "coming back to the project"]
Already tried: Refresh, Shift + Refresh, a hard browser refresh, a private window
First red line in the Console: [paste it]
Last version that worked: [the chat message whose Preview still works]
Find the cause and explain it to me before you change any code.

## Still stuck?

Create a new empty Lovable project and open its preview. If the empty project works and yours doesn't, the problem is in your project's code or settings, so read the Console of your own project (section 2). If the empty one fails too, the problem is your browser, your network or Lovable: try the private window from section 1, then another network (a phone hotspot is enough), then the status page.

guides.t: Lovable publish not working or changes not showing
guides.d: Lovable app won't publish or the live site doesn't change? Match what the Publish dialog shows to its cause, including database errors that block it.
guides.x:
Fix guide · updated 2026-11-09

## Lovable publish not working: changes not showing, Publishing failed, or no Publish button

Publishing failed · Fix build errors · latest changes not on the live site

You clicked Publish in Lovable and nothing changed on your live site. Or the dialog shows Publishing failed, or there's no Publish button at all. Each of these has a short list of causes, and the Publish dialog (top right of the editor) usually tells you which one. Find what you see below.

## 1. The live site doesn't show your latest changes

This is the most common one, and nothing is broken. Lovable's docs explain that publishing deploys a copy of your project as it was at that moment. Everything you change afterwards stays in the editor until you publish again: click Publish, then Publish changes. A small dot on the Publish button means you have changes the live site doesn't have yet. Accepting a draft is not publishing either: its edits join your unpublished changes.

If the dialog said Your website was updated and you still see the old version:

- Reload without the browser's cache (Ctrl+Shift+R, or Cmd+Shift+R on a Mac), or open the site in a private window.

- Check that you're opening the exact published address. The lovable.app address uses your project's URL subdomain, which can differ from the project's name, and changing the subdomain moves the site to a new address.

- On a custom domain, DNS changes can take time. If the domain itself doesn't work, see Lovable custom domain not working.

If the live site opens on a blank page instead, see Lovable blank page or 404 after deploy.

If the live site is up to date and something on it is broken while the preview works, see Lovable published site not working.

## 2. The dialog shows "Fix build errors"

Instead of the publish button, the dialog shows Try to fix. Your latest changes failed to build, so publishing them would fail the same way. Click Try to fix and Lovable will try to fix it in the chat, or fix the error yourself, then publish once the preview builds. To read the real error and fix the common ones, see Lovable build unsuccessful.

## 3. A "Publishing failed" banner

The banner says which kind of failure it is. Lovable's docs list these, with what to do:

- A temporary issue, like a timeout or a rate limit on a connected service. Click Try again; retries usually work.

- An error in your app: a build error, or an edge function that couldn't be deployed. For a build error, the banner shows a short summary of it. Click Try to fix. If your edge functions fail once they're live, see Edge Function returned a non-2xx status code.

- A configuration issue in your project, for example a file too large to include. Click Try to fix.

- An external connection or secret that needs your attention, like an expired Supabase connection or a connected service that reached its plan limits. Lovable can't change those for you: reconnect the service or update its plan, then click Try again.

- A database change that conflicts with existing data. The banner shows the database's own error message. See the next section.

- An internal error on Lovable's side. Try again in a few minutes. If it keeps failing, contact Lovable support with your project link.

## 4. A database change conflicts with your live data

A change can work while you build and still fail when you publish, because your live database already holds rows that break it. We reproduced the usual cases on Postgres 16. Supabase databases run on Postgres, so the messages are the same. Here's what each one needs:

column "username" of relation "profiles" contains null values. A new required column was added, and the rows you already have don't have a value for it. Give the column a default, or add it as optional, fill in the existing rows, then make it required:

alter table public.profiles add column username text not null default '';

could not create unique index "profiles_email_key", with Key (email)=(a@x.test) is duplicated. The change makes a column unique, and some rows already share a value. Find them, decide which row to keep, then publish again:

select email, count(*) from public.profiles
group by email having count(*) > 1;

insert or update on table "orders" violates foreign key constraint "orders_profile_id_fkey", with Key (profile_id)=(99) is not present in table "profiles". The change links two tables, and some rows point to something that no longer exists. Find them:

select o.* from public.orders o
where not exists (select 1 from public.profiles p where p.id = o.profile_id);

invalid input syntax for type integer: "free". A column changes type, and some rows hold values that can't be converted. Clean up those values first, or keep the old type.

For this kind of failure, Lovable's banner offers Ask Lovable, and Lovable confirms with you before changing anything, since the fix touches real data. Read what it proposes before you agree. Deleting the rows that get in the way makes the error go away fastest, and it also deletes your users' data. If rows have to change, know which ones, and keep a copy first.

## 5. No Publish button, or you can't click it

- Narrow window: the button collapses to an icon without a label, next to Share.

- "You don't have permission to publish this project" when you hover it: publishing needs editor access or above. Ask the project's owner or a workspace admin.

- "Approval needed" or "Publishing blocked": an Enterprise workspace policy requires an admin's approval, or doesn't allow this kind of publishing. Use Request approval, or ask an admin.

## 6. People can't open the live app, or it asks them to log in

The row under the website address in the Publish dialog sets who can see the site. Public, the default, lets anyone with the link in. With Invite only on the Free and Pro plans, only the people you add can open it, after logging in, up to 10 per project. On Business and Enterprise plans, Workspace limits it to logged-in workspace members. A change of audience only takes effect when you click Publish or Publish changes.

## 7. The site was live and went offline

Published sites don't expire. Lovable may unpublish a project in a Free workspace after about a year with no visits, no owner login and no edits. An app that uses Lovable's built-in backend or AI features also needs credits available to keep answering requests. Publishing itself is free, but asking Lovable to publish from the chat uses credits like any other request.

## Still stuck?

Write down the exact words of the banner, including the build or database error it shows, and what you changed since the last publish that worked. That's what anyone helping you will ask for first, and the change since the last good publish is usually where the problem is.

guides.t: Lovable site "Not secure": browser warning and scan fixes
guides.d: Live Lovable site shows Not secure, too many redirects or Dangerous site, or the publish scan flags critical issues? What each means and the fix.
guides.x:
Fix guide · updated 2026-11-11

## Lovable published site "Not secure" (browser warning or security scan)

Not secure · Your connection is not private · ERR_TOO_MANY_REDIRECTS · Dangerous site · 2 critical security issues found

"Not secure" can mean two different problems on a Lovable app. The first is the browser: it doesn't trust the connection to your address, so it shows a label next to the address, or a warning page instead of your app. The second is Lovable's own security scan, which says your app has holes, for example "2 critical security issues found" when you publish. The first is about your address. The second is about your data, and the padlock says nothing about it. Lovable's docs say every published URL is served over HTTPS with a certificate Lovable sets up, custom domains included. So when the browser complains, something between your visitor and Lovable isn't finished yet, or points to the wrong place.

## First: what exactly do you see?

- "Not secure" next to the address, and the page loads: the page came over plain http://. Section 1.

- A warning page instead of your site: "Your connection is not private" in Chrome, "This Connection Is Not Private" in Safari, "Warning: Potential Security Risk Ahead" in Firefox, often with a code like NET::ERR_CERT_COMMON_NAME_INVALID. The certificate doesn't cover this address yet. Section 2.

- "This page isn't working" and "redirected you too many times" (ERR_TOO_MANY_REDIRECTS): almost always Cloudflare in front of Lovable. Section 3.

- A red page titled "Dangerous site" or "Deceptive site ahead": Google flagged your address. Section 4.

- The publish dialog says "2 critical security issues found" or "3 security findings": that's Lovable's scan of your app, not the browser. Section 5.

- Visitors land on a page titled "Website Takedown Notice": Lovable's Trust & Safety team blocked the site. Nothing below applies. Contact Lovable support.

## 1. "Not secure" next to the address

Lovable's hosting doesn't leave visitors on plain http://. We checked a live Lovable site: a visit to http:// gets a permanent redirect to https://, and the answer tells the browser to use only HTTPS for that address for the next year. Addresses ending in .lovable.app are also on the list of HTTPS-only domains built into the major browsers, so a browser never even tries them over http://.

So a grey "Not secure" label means the page didn't come from Lovable's hosting. Two usual reasons:

- Your domain still points to your old host, or to your registrar's parking page. Look at the page. Is it really your Lovable app, in its latest version? If you see your old site or a "this domain is registered" page, your DNS records still send visitors somewhere else. Follow Lovable custom domain not working, sections 2 and 5.

- Your domain goes through Cloudflare with encryption turned off. In Cloudflare's SSL/TLS settings, the encryption mode says Off. Cloudflare's docs say this mode "redirects any HTTPS request to plaintext HTTP". Change it to Full (section 3 explains why not Flexible).

If you clicked past a warning page earlier, Chrome also shows "Not secure", in red, with https crossed out. That's a certificate problem: go to section 2.

The padlock is fine, but an image, a script or a call to your API fails. That's mixed content: your page is on https:// and asks for something on http://. According to MDN, today's browsers upgrade images, video and audio to https:// by themselves and block every other kind of request. If the address is an IP number, even images are blocked. Open the Console (right-click → Inspect → Console) and look for lines that start with Mixed Content:. Each one names the blocked address. A typical case: an automation webhook on your own server, like http://203.0.113.7:5678/webhook/…. Your published site can't call it until that server has a domain name and a certificate. Once it does, ask Lovable to replace every http:// address in the code with https://.

## 2. "Your connection is not private"

The browser got a certificate that doesn't match the address, or no certificate at all. Lovable creates the certificate for you once your DNS records are right. You don't buy one, and Lovable's docs say a certificate from your registrar (Namecheap, GoDaddy and so on) "is not used by Lovable's hosting". Check these in order.

The domain's status. Open Project → Settings → Domains. Until your domain shows Active, the warning is expected. Setting up domain and Finishing up mean Lovable is still checking your records or issuing the certificate. DNS changes can take up to 72 hours to spread. If there's still no certificate after 72 hours, Lovable's docs ask you to contact support.

The other half of your address. Only www.yourdomain.com fails, or only yourdomain.com? When you connect a root domain, the option Redirect www.yourdomain.com → yourdomain.com is on by default, and the domain row shows www included once both addresses work. If you turned the option off, Lovable connected only the root domain, so www has no certificate from Lovable. Connect www.yourdomain.com as well. With the option on, the setup window lists records for both addresses: add both at your DNS provider.

CAA records. These list which companies may issue certificates for your domain. If your domain has CAA records that leave Lovable's certificate companies out, the domain stays on Finishing up or shows a connection warning. Lovable's docs recommend allowing all three companies it uses: Google Trust Services, Let's Encrypt and SSL.com.

0 issue "pki.goog"
0 issue "letsencrypt.org"
0 issue "ssl.com"

Add these at your DNS provider (flag 0, tag issue, the company's domain as the value), or remove your CAA records if nobody needs them anymore. Connecting a subdomain? Check the root domain too, because a subdomain without CAA records of its own follows the root's. Then open the domain's three-dots menu and select Check again.

Only you, or only one network, sees the warning. Open the site on your phone with Wi-Fi off. If it works there, the problem is on your side. Check the date and time on your computer: a wrong clock makes every certificate look expired, and Chrome then shows NET::ERR_CERT_DATE_INVALID. An antivirus that inspects HTTPS, or a company network that does the same, can also cause the warning.

## 3. "Redirected you too many times" behind Cloudflare

Lovable's hosting sends every http:// request to https://. If Cloudflare's proxy sits in front (orange cloud) and its encryption mode is Flexible, Cloudflare talks to Lovable over plain http://. Lovable answers "use https", Cloudflare asks again over http://, and so on, forever. Cloudflare's docs describe this exact loop: "Redirect loops will occur if your origin server automatically redirects all HTTP requests to HTTPS."

Two ways out. Pick one.

- Keep Cloudflare's proxy. Set the encryption mode to Full, the fix Cloudflare's docs give for this loop. Once your domain shows Active in Lovable, you can move to Full (strict), which also checks Lovable's certificate. In Lovable, the domain should be connected with Advanced → Uses Cloudflare or similar proxy turned on. That mode uses a CNAME record pointing to your project's published address, and Lovable issues the certificates once that record is right. Lovable's docs are clear that in this mode the proxy setup is yours: Lovable doesn't configure, validate or monitor it.

- Drop the proxy. Set the DNS records for your Lovable domain to DNS only (grey cloud). Lovable gives the same fix for Cloudflare errors 1001 and 1003.

More on Cloudflare in Lovable custom domain not working, section 3.

## 4. A red "Dangerous site" page

This page comes from Google Safe Browsing. Google decided the address hosts phishing (a page that tricks people into typing their passwords or card numbers) or something harmful. Chrome, and the other browsers that use Google's list, now warn every visitor. Your certificate isn't the problem, and no setting in Lovable removes the warning. Only Google removes it, after a review.

- Confirm it. Paste your address into Google's Safe Browsing site status page. If you use both your lovable.app address and your own domain, check both.

- Get access to Google's report. Add your site to Google Search Console and verify it. Lovable's Google Search Console connector can do the verification for you. Once it's connected, ask in the project chat: "Verify my Lovable app's domain in Google Search Console." It adds the verification tag to your app's HTML, publishes it, and completes the check with Google.

- Read the report and fix everything. In Search Console, Security & Manual Actions → Security issues names the problem and gives example pages. Fix every issue it lists, on every page it names.

- Request a review. When everything is fixed, select Request Review in the same report and describe what you changed. Google says a review takes from a few days to a few weeks.

## 5. Lovable's scan says your app isn't secure

When you open the publish dialog, Lovable runs a Quick scan that takes about 10 seconds. It checks your database access rules (including row-level security mistakes), your dependencies, and MCP server exposure. The dialog then shows No security issues found, or a count such as 2 critical security issues found. From Lovable's docs: "Findings do not block publishing by default, but you should resolve critical issues before making your app available." If your workspace admin turned on Block publishing with critical issues, you can't publish until the critical findings are resolved.

- Click the scan line to open the Security view. Critical means problems that need your attention immediately. Warning means issues to review and fix if necessary.

- Try to fix on a finding asks Lovable to fix it. Try to fix all sends every open finding in one request. Test your app before you publish the result: a rule that locks the data too tightly breaks the app in a new way, for example with "new row violates row-level security policy" or "permission denied for table".

- The publish dialog doesn't run the Deep scan. Run it from the Security view before you launch. It reviews all your code for problems like exposed secrets, unsafe input handling and authorization gaps. It takes about 4 minutes on a small app and up to 15 on a large one.

Keep the difference in mind: the padlock only means the connection is encrypted. A site with a perfect padlock can still let any visitor read every row of your tables. For the checks a scanner can't do for you, like using your app as a logged-out visitor and as a second user, see the security checklist for vibe-coded apps.

## What to send Lovable

Start in the project chat: ask Lovable about the domain. Its docs say it reports the domain's state, how long it has been in that state, which DNS records it expects and whether it can see them. If you need support, send these lines:

Address: https://yourdomain.com (and https://www.yourdomain.com)
Browser message: [the exact text and code, e.g. NET::ERR_CERT_COMMON_NAME_INVALID]
Status in Project → Settings → Domains: [Active / Setting up domain / Finishing up]
DNS managed at: [provider] · Cloudflare proxy: [on / off] · encryption mode: [Off / Flexible / Full / Full (strict)]
Seen by: [everyone / only me / only on one network]
Since: [date and time, and what changed just before]

## Still stuck?

Open your site on a phone with Wi-Fi off. If it works there, the problem is your computer, its network or its antivirus (end of section 2). If it fails there too, the problem is your domain's setup or a Google flag, so go back to the list at the top. And until your domain shows Active, your lovable.app address keeps showing your app with a valid padlock: share that one while you wait. Lovable only starts sending visitors from it to your own domain once that domain is Active and set as primary.
